note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Paul quotes this straight from Jeremiah: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah”. Christians avoid that, because when you ask them who the new covenant is for, it tells you crystal clear right there who it was for: the house of Israel and the house of Judah. He separates us like that because there was a split into two kingdoms, and when he says Israel right there, he means all 12 tribes.

“Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt”. That was the old covenant, animal sacrifice. The 12 tribes are the bride and God is the husband. “because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord”: meaning we went into slavery.

“I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people”. This is kingdom, the same promise Jeremiah gave. So this is the answer to replacement theology, the answer to supersessionism. The new covenant was never given to a church that took Israel's place; it was made with the same Israel that broke the first one.

And Jeremiah goes on to seal it: if the ordinances of the sun, the moon and the stars depart, then the seed of Israel ceases from being a nation. They have not departed, so the 12 tribes are still here to this day. Even in Paul's time the 12 tribes were there, yet Christians cannot point them out in the New Testament and say they are lost. It's all a lie. This is where Paul was getting it from.

precepts.text: Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: see that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount. Everything Moses did was symbolic of what he saw in the heavens.
precepts.point: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ. All those sacrifices were a shadow of things to come.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
The priests under the law were those “Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.”

Everything Moses did was symbolic of what he saw in the heavens. The tabernacle, the service and the sacrifices were made after a pattern shown to him in the mount; they were an example and a shadow, not the heavenly things themselves.

That is what Colossians means: “Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” The service Moses set up was a pattern pointing to the real thing, and the real thing is Christ. So no man should judge you or beguile you back into the shadow when the body has come.

precepts.text: The bond of the covenant is the new covenant. I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts. We are going to know God's laws and we will keep them. You are not going to forget the feast day and eat the donut out of routine; his laws will be in our minds, and we will do them and serve him. We are in the beginning of the new covenant now, but once Christ returns it will be fully established in the wilderness. And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest, because the Lord is going to teach us.
precepts.point: I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me: those that break God's laws, those that got leaven in them. I will bring them forth out of the country where they sojourn, and they shall not enter into the land of Israel. You will be delivered up out of that destruction, but the same way everybody was delivered up from Egypt and everybody did not make it into the promised land, there will be groups of people that will be delivered that will not make it into the promised land.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness

precepts.why:
Ezekiel says, “I will cause you to pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant”. The rod is correction. And the bond of the covenant is the new covenant in Hebrews: “For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord”. After those days means after we are delivered out of here, out of this new Egypt, America.

“I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people”. Meaning we are going to know God's laws and we will keep God's laws. Right now it can be routine: you go to work every day, stop in the donut store for a donut and your coffee, eat the donut, and then remember, damn, it's the days of unleavened bread, how could I forget? But the Lord God says his laws will be in our minds. We are not going to forget, and we will do them and serve him. That is the new covenant. We are in the beginning of it now, but once Christ returns it will be fully established in the wilderness.

“And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest.” All of us will know the Lord, from the least amongst us to the greatest. You won't have to go and teach anybody, because the Lord is going to teach us. Every custom and thought we learned in America has to go, and he will show us even the parts we are missing now, like the sun and the moon working together for the times and seasons, wisdom destroyed from amongst us through slavery.

So being brought into the bond of the covenant is us being purged in the wilderness again. As he pleaded with our fathers and got rid of the leaven from amongst them, he will “purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me”: those that break God's laws, those with leaven in them. Many will be delivered out of here, but not everyone is going to make it into the promised land. Those who enter will have his laws written in their hearts.

precepts.text: Behold, the days come when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah, and I will put my laws into their mind and write them in their hearts. He does not say Gentiles there. All through the New Testament it is Jew and Gentile, Jew and Greek, and here he makes plain who he means: the two kingdoms that split in the book of Kings. The Jews and the Gentiles are Judah and Israel.
precepts.point: The scholars know the western diaspora Paul travelled to was the Greek-speaking Jewish diaspora, the places named in Acts 2 and Acts 13 and in his letters; they had no Hebrew or Aramaic and their Torah and prayers were in Greek from the third century before Christ. It is black Christians who do not understand that Paul went to Israelites.

note.label: The Fallacy of Black Christians

precepts.text: The priests serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished to make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.
precepts.point: What was built in the wilderness was a shadow of what is in the heavens. The Most High is the architect, and He showed Moses the pattern of a heavenly tabernacle to be made for Israel on earth; thy kingdom come, thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven, is an example of that same order.

note.label: Exodus 26: The Pattern Shown in the Mount

precepts.why:
The boards of shittim wood, the sockets of silver and the bars overlaid with gold are the physical structure of the tabernacle, how it would be put together and what it would consist of. Then: “And thou shalt rear up the tabernacle according to the fashion thereof which was shewed thee in the mount.” Hebrews tells what that fashion was: the priests “serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.”

What was built in the wilderness was a shadow of what is in the heavens. The Most High showed Moses all of this in mount Sinai; the forty days and forty nights were not the ten commandments alone. Moses came down with a whole architectural layout based on what the Most High showed him. The Most High is the architect, and He showed Moses the pattern of a heavenly tabernacle to be made for Israel on earth.

precepts.text: Moses was warned to make all things according to the pattern shown in the mount, not after the fashion of the nations.
precepts.point: Ahaz moves the brazen altar and commands Urijah to make the new altar the place of all the offerings, keeping the brazen altar for himself to inquire by.

note.label: 2 Kings 16: Ahaz and the Altar of Damascus

precepts.why:
The priests “serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.”

The true altar was made after the pattern of heavenly things given through Moses. Ahaz went to Damascus to meet the king of Assyria, saw a heathen altar he admired, and sent Urijah the priest “the fashion of the altar, and the pattern of it, according to all the workmanship thereof.” He traded the pattern shown in the mount for the fashion of the nations.

Then he moved the brasen altar from before the Lord, made the new altar the place of all the offerings, and kept the brasen altar “for me to enquire by.” Moses was warned to make all things according to the pattern, and Ahaz did the opposite.

precepts.text: The same words carried into the new testament: a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.
precepts.point: This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you. Testament and covenant are the same word, and the scripture names who that covenant was made with.

note.label: Luke 22: The Passover, the Betrayal, and the Denial

precepts.why:
The same words Jeremiah wrote are carried into the new testament. “For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah”.

So the new testament Christ named at the table, in his blood shed for you, is the new covenant of Jeremiah 31, and it is made with the house of Israel and the house of Judah. Jeremiah and Hebrews say the same thing; the covenant did not change who it was made with.

precepts.text: The same covenant with the house of Israel, forgiving their unrighteousness and remembering their sins no more.
precepts.point: Remission of sins, the forgiveness and canceling of the debt, is the new covenant made with the house of Israel, not with every nation. The Most High promised to forgive Israel's iniquity and remember their sins no more.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
The same covenant is written again in Hebrews: “For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts.”

“For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.” It is the house of Israel whose sins are remembered no more. Remission of sins belongs to that covenant.

precepts.point: That is why Christ is called the end of the law (of sacrifice) to them that believe. Ephesians 2:14-16 shows Christ broke down the middle wall of partition between the two kingdoms, abolishing in his flesh the enmity (the law of commandments contained in ordinances, meaning the sacrificial laws), making of twain one new man.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Christ hath “obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises. For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.”

The new covenant is made “with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah”, both kingdoms, “Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant.” The false brethren wanted to bring the brethren back into the first covenant of circumcision and sacrifice; the liberty in Christ Jesus is the better covenant, which takes in the northern kingdom that the first could never save.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 7 Sealing The 144k

precepts.why: “I will put my laws into their mind”: putting his law in our minds is what the seal makes reference to.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Breakdown Of Revelation 16

precepts.why: “We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens”: the Lord sitting in his majesty, in the heavens. “A minister of the sanctuary”: there is a sanctuary in heaven. “And of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man”: there is a tabernacle up there, pitched by the Lord and not made by man. You better believe it.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Breakdown Of Revelation 16

precepts.why: “Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things”: Paul speaks of what the priests do on the earth, then reveals a mystery. The temple, the sanctuary, the ark of the covenant, what Moses set up and what King Solomon built, are a shadow of the heavenly. “As Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 4 Kingdom Vision

precepts.why: “Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things”. Moses was admonished when he was about to make the tabernacle to make all things according to the pattern shown in the mount. The tabernacle came before the temple. Its furnishings were the example and shadow of things in heaven, explaining why John's vision contains what God commanded Moses to make on earth.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 14 Part 1

precepts.why: This goes with Isaiah 8:16 and Revelation 7 regarding the seal in the foreheads. “With the house of Israel and with the house of Judah”: because we were split into two kingdoms. “Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers”: not according to animal sacrifice; that was the old covenant. “And I regarded them not”: he sent us into captivity. “I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts”: that’s the point; that is what being sealed in our foreheads means. Verse 11, “And they shall not teach every man his neighbour,” is clearly talking about the kingdom. People try to say verse 11 is for today; it’s not for today.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 14 Part 2

precepts.why: “For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind”. That is what we are being sealed with: God’s laws. If you are in here and you don’t believe you have to keep God’s laws, you are in the wrong place.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 9 Explained Pt. 1

precepts.why: Paul discussed the seal too. “I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts”: the law going into our mind is what being sealed is. The men that don’t have the seal of God are these other nations, the locusts.

points: In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. The old covenant of animal sacrifice became obsolete upon Christ's crucifixion, because he was the Lamb of God, that ultimate sacrifice for the nation of Israel, bringing in the new covenant.

The problem is not merely that something old is being replaced. The problem arises when people refuse to accept that God is moving forward. That's when the agony of defeat comes in: you can't accept that God is using a particular person, people, or organization for a greater purpose because they're more effective. God doesn't want the old; he wants to use the new.

Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah. Both kingdoms are mentioned right here.

The power has been in God's laws the whole time.
